rows.title: Policy divergence
rows.figure: Fed Oct hold ~84%, Dec hike ~90%; ECB Oct hold, Dec hike likely; BoE Nov ~95%; BoJ Oct <5%, Dec ~80%; BoC Oct ~1 in 4; RBA Nov ~1 in 3; RBNZ Oct 28 close call
rows.read: Nearly every central bank is holding this month and pointing at a hike later, so the race is about who moves first. The Bank of England looks closest, while Canada's soft core inflation and Japan's caution pushed their next hikes further out. Currencies whose banks look ready to act, like the pound, have the edge.

rows.title: Growth differentials
rows.figure: China Q3 GDP 4.5% (fc 4.4%); US NAHB 29 (fc 31, lowest since 2012); BoC BOS -0.33 (prior -0.38)
rows.read: China grew a little faster than expected, which helped the currencies that sell to it, like the Australian dollar. In the US, high mortgage rates are hurting housing, and Canadian firms grew gloomier after trade talks collapsed. Growth is uneven, but it isn't yet weak enough to change central banks' plans.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: Canada CPI 3.1% (fc 3.2%), trim 1.8%, median 1.9%; Canada 5-yr expectations ~3.9% (3.4%); UK CPI Wed fc 3.4%; NZ Q3 CPI Wed fc 3.8%; Japan CPI Fri
rows.read: Canada's inflation came in a little soft, and its core measures are back below the 2% target, so energy is doing most of the work there. But people now expect more inflation, and oil turned higher again today, which keeps central banks wary. This week's UK, New Zealand and Japan reports decide how much more pressure they face.

rows.title: Risk sentiment
rows.figure: Iran says US hit Konarak base (unconfirmed); Houthis claim 6 attacks on Saudi sites in 48h; European stocks -1.1 to -1.6%; Nasdaq 100 ~+1.25%
rows.read: The calm broke in the afternoon when Iran said the US struck one of its naval bases, and the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi oil sites. France's unrest weighed on European markets, while US tech stocks bounced. Fear is now coming from two places at once, which keeps a floor under safe havens like the franc.

rows.title: Terms of trade / commodities
rows.read: Oil fell in the morning on the Russia sanctions waiver, then turned higher on the new Gulf attacks. Expensive oil helps exporters like Canada and costs importers like Japan and the euro area. It also lifts yields, which is why gold fell on a day with more conflict news.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Oct 13: hedge funds against CAD (sharply added), against EUR (added), for AUD (trimmed; real money strongly against), against JPY (real money for), oil bets near weakest since 2015
rows.read: Hedge funds are betting most heavily against the Canadian dollar and added to bets against the euro, which France's trouble rewarded today. They still lean toward the Australian dollar while long-term investors bet against it, so a bad turn in risk mood could hit it fast. In the yen and the Aussie, the two groups disagree.

rows.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk
rows.figure: OAT–Bund ~141bp (high ~146bp); French 10Y ~4.9%; France revenue vote Tue, Moody's Fri; US FY26 deficit $1.99T
rows.read: France is the fiscal story this week: investors sold French bonds and stocks together, which signals worry about its finances rather than ordinary caution. That pushes the euro down through higher borrowing costs. The US deficit is large too, but for now it shows up in higher yields rather than a weaker dollar.
